body: After seeing many tests that are written in the same way (unmodified, add an entry, do not override namespace entries), I wonder if it would have been feasible to write **one** getWidgetState utility with configuration parameters and unit test that one instead, delegating calls to every widgets afterwards and only checking how we call it from widgets.
this was no more used maybe?
Some tests are identical indeed. But not all, do you have a proposal for making both special tests and generic ones?
Yes exactly and it hadn't been removed.
After more carefully looking at `getWidgetState` implementations indeed it seems pretty different between widgets and not something easily made generic so all good

It's a boolean flag that expresses the default value of the hitsPerPage. It is a reserved keyword indeed https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/scripting/javascript/reference/javascript-reserved-words but we're safe https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Lexical_grammar#Reserved_word_usage
no need for `...args` here because there's no constructor
~should be 4 given the test I believe~

body: You use Snapshot for those cases but I find them tedious in that case. Because by reading the tests file we have no clue of what it's expected.

If one of the `lowerBound` or `upperBound` is `=== ''` then it will end like this:

* `xx:` or `:xx`

Is it expected?
Yes
OK will had a more precise test.
The previous comment the Snapshot is more accurate in that case because the structure of `SearchParameters` is way more complicated than the `uiState` one.
Maybe we can rename this to `getWidgetState(fullUiState, { searchParam })` to better understand what's inside and map to getWidgetSearchParameters?

Note for myself and anyone: this test checks this user flow:
- user loads https://website/search
- user clicks on page 4
- user click on back button
- we load page 0
We can get rid of the condition by doing a filter before the reduce.
Could we wrap this condition with brackets?
